candidates.original_title: Does darkness lead to happiness? Masked suffix priming effects
candidates.description: Masked suffix priming facilitates processing of complex words relative to simple words in adults through overlapping suffixes between prime and target
candidates.citation_sentence: This first experiment replicates the study by Dunabeitia, [20], but with our own stimuli and in child and adult populations.
candidates.notes: The adult results replicate the original Dunabeitia et al. (2008) finding, but fourth and fifth graders show no morphological effect while sixth graders show a marginal effect, yielding a mixed pattern across age groups within one experiment.
